1Password review: digital legacy verdict

By the Afterkeep research team · Reviewed on 15 Oct 2026

Verdict: Excellent password manager, but it has no automatic emergency-access feature. Legacy planning relies on the Emergency Kit and family account recovery. Best for: Families who will store the Emergency Kit with their will and use a Families plan, where an organiser can help recover members' accounts.

Key facts

  • Category: Vaults & password managers
  • Pricing: Paid plans only (free trial). Check current pricing.
  • Best for: Families who will store the Emergency Kit with their will and use a Families plan, where an organiser can help recover members' accounts.
  • Printable Emergency Kit with your sign-in details and Secret Key
  • Families plan lets organisers recover family members' accounts

Official site / docs ↗

What are the pros and cons of 1Password?

Pros

  • Printable Emergency Kit with your sign-in details and Secret Key
  • Families plan lets organisers recover family members' accounts
  • Strong security model and polished apps

Cons

  • No time-delayed emergency contact feature
  • The Emergency Kit has to be stored securely and kept current
  • No free tier

What are similar tools?

Vaults & password managers

Bitwarden

The best-value password manager with real emergency access: trusted contacts can request View or Takeover access after a wait time you set.

Vaults & password managers

Keeper

A solid choice with built-in Emergency Access: name trusted contacts who can request your vault after a wait period.

Vaults & password managers

LastPass Emergency Access

It works: contacts can request vault access after a wait period. LastPass's 2022 security breaches are a good reason to look at alternatives first, though.
